question.problem: The remainder of dividing $p(x)=9{x}^{5}-3{x}^{4}-2x-\frac{1}{3}$ by $1-3x$ is{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
The remainder theorem states that when $p(x)$ is divided by $(1-3x)=-3(x-\frac{1}{3}),$ the remainder equals $p(\frac{1}{3}).$ 

Evaluating $p(\frac{1}{3})$ directly gives

$$
\begin{aligned}p(\frac{1}{3}) & =9\cdot {(\frac{1}{3})}^{5}-3\cdot {(\frac{1}{3})}^{4}-2\cdot (\frac{1}{3})-\frac{1}{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{27}-\frac{1}{27}-\frac{2}{3}-\frac{1}{3} \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the remainder of dividing $p(x)=9{x}^{5}-3{x}^{4}-2x-\frac{1}{3}$ by $1-3x$ is $-1.$

**Note:** We can check the answer by carrying out synthetic division:

|  | ${x}^{5}$ | ${x}^{4}$ | ${x}^{3}$ | ${x}^{2}$ | ${x}^{1}$ | ${x}^{0}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\frac{1}{3}$ | $9$ | $-3$ | $0$ | $0$ | $-2$ | $-\frac{1}{3}$ |
|  | $↓$ | $3$ | $0$ | $0$ | $0$ | $-\frac{2}{3}$ |
|  | $9$ | $0$ | $0$ | $0$ | $-2$ | $-1$ |
